stories.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp Is Now Live on the DeepSeek API Platform
stories.paragraph: DeepSeek has released DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, a vision-capable model, to its API platform. The release marks an expansion of DeepSeek's multimodal offerings under the V4 model family. As an experimental release, it signals ongoing development work rather than a finalized product, and follows the company's pattern of incremental API rollouts to gather real-world usage data.

stories.title: Ox Alpha
stories.paragraph: OpenRouter has listed a model called Ox Alpha, attributed to a stealth developer, on its model routing platform. The listing is notable because OpenRouter serves as an aggregator for many third-party models, and stealth listings occasionally precede public announcements from new AI labs. Few technical details have been disclosed, leaving the model's architecture, parameter count, and intended use cases unspecified at launch.

stories.title: Micron announces $10B research hub in Boise
stories.paragraph: Micron Technology has announced a $10 billion research facility in Boise, Idaho, branded as Micron Research Labs, focused on long-horizon innovation in memory and AI infrastructure. The investment underscores the growing demand for advanced memory systems in AI workloads, where high-bandwidth memory has become a critical bottleneck for large model training and inference. Boise is already home to Micron's existing operations, making the new hub an extension of the company's established presence in the region.

stories.title: Introducing AI Futures
stories.paragraph: OpenAI has launched an initiative called AI Futures, aimed at shaping longer-term thinking about the societal direction of artificial intelligence development. The program appears to be a policy and engagement effort rather than a product release, continuing OpenAI's practice of publishing position pieces and funding external research on AI's broader implications. The announcement comes at a time when regulatory discussions around AI governance are intensifying in multiple jurisdictions.

stories.title: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale
stories.paragraph: Researcher Simon Willison reports that ChatGPT's search functionality has begun using the site: operator at scale when retrieving web results, a behavior tracked by a tool called Promptwatch. Promptwatch is part of the emerging Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) space, which is analogous to traditional SEO but focused on improving a website's representation in AI-generated responses. The finding has practical implications for publishers and marketers, as it suggests ChatGPT's retrieval pipeline can be deliberately influenced by domain-level targeting in ways similar to conventional search engines.

stories.title: Young Americans increasingly fear AI will take their jobs
stories.paragraph: A Pew Research Center survey finds that young adults in the United States are growing more concerned that AI will displace them from the workforce, with anxiety levels rising compared to prior years. The data is notable because younger cohorts have historically been more optimistic about technology adoption, making this shift a meaningful reversal in sentiment. Pew's findings add empirical weight to ongoing policy debates about labor market protections in an era of rapid AI-driven automation.

stories.title: Protesters haul a guillotine to city council meeting about an AI data center
stories.paragraph: Protesters brought a guillotine to a city council meeting in which a proposed AI data center was being discussed, escalating local opposition to the point where a company representative was escorted out by police after reportedly feeling unsafe. The incident illustrates the increasingly charged public atmosphere surrounding data center development, which communities often associate with high energy consumption, water usage, and job displacement. The developer has not publicly confirmed whether the project will proceed.

stories.title: Copyright does not protect AI-generated content in EU
stories.paragraph: A post circulating on Mathstodon highlights the EU's legal position that copyright protection does not extend to content generated solely by AI systems, consistent with the principle that copyright requires human authorship. This stance aligns with similar rulings in the United States, where the Copyright Office has declined to register purely AI-generated works. The issue carries commercial significance for companies seeking to assert ownership over AI-produced text, images, and code.

stories.title: Show HN: Huzzah – a novel approach to coding with AI
stories.paragraph: Developer Daniel Vaughn has released an experimental code editor called Huzzah, designed to reduce the verbosity required when working with AI coding agents. Vaughn describes frustration with having to write full natural-language sentences for every code change, and Huzzah attempts to address this through a more compact, gesture-like interaction model. The project is in early experimental stages and was built out of personal use beginning in early 2026.

stories.title: Show HN: Kandelo – a POSIX-compatible multi-process WASM kernel for the browser
stories.paragraph: Kandelo is an open-source, WebAssembly-based kernel that enables POSIX-compatible multi-process programs to run inside browsers and Node.js environments. The project is being evaluated as the underlying runtime for WordPress Playground, which runs server-side WordPress entirely in the browser without a traditional server. While still experimental, Kandelo can already execute a broad range of existing software compiled to WebAssembly, making it relevant to efforts to bring AI and server-side tooling to edge and offline contexts.

stories.title: AI companies destroy physical books – let's scan rare books before it's too late
stories.paragraph: Anna's Archive has published a blog post alleging that AI companies are physically destroying books in the process of scanning them for training data, and calling for urgent digitization of rare volumes before they are lost. The post does not name specific companies but describes destructive scanning practices in which book spines are cut to enable high-throughput page scanning. The Archive frames the issue as a preservation emergency, arguing that rare and out-of-print books face permanent physical loss even as their content may be absorbed into proprietary AI systems.

stories.title: Are you good at AI, or just using it?
stories.paragraph: A team is soliciting public feedback on a proposed six-level proficiency ladder for individual AI skill, ranging from L0 (no experience) to higher levels that involve agentic workflows, multi-model orchestration, and systematic prompt engineering. The framework attempts to distinguish passive AI consumption from active, expert-level use, a distinction that has practical implications for hiring, training, and self-assessment. The initiative reflects growing interest in standardizing AI literacy benchmarks as the tools become ubiquitous in professional settings.

stories.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
stories.paragraph: Researchers introduced ConceptGuard, a benchmark designed to evaluate machine unlearning in LLMs under context-sensitive conditions that existing benchmarks ignore. Current unlearning evaluations rely on disjoint forget and retain sets of independent facts and measure success through simple factual recall, a framing that fails to capture how knowledge is interconnected in real usage. ConceptGuard tests whether a model that forgets a target fact also appropriately handles contextually related information, raising the bar for what constitutes successful unlearning. The work highlights a gap between reported benchmark performance and the practical safety guarantees that selective knowledge removal is meant to provide.

stories.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.paragraph: AI4AI-Bench is a new benchmark that evaluates whether LLM agents can propose improvements to the training algorithms used to produce AI systems, a process the authors frame as recursive self-improvement (RSI). The benchmark focuses on the training algorithm itself — objective functions and update rules — because a better algorithm improves the compute-to-capability ratio for every subsequent training run. By measuring agent performance on algorithmic design tasks, the work provides an empirical handle on whether current LLMs can meaningfully participate in their own improvement cycle. The benchmark is notable because it operationalizes a concept that has largely remained theoretical in AI safety discussions.

stories.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
stories.paragraph: Researchers at arXiv proposed MidTool, a data synthesis method applied during the mid-training stage of LLM development to improve general tool-use capabilities. Prior work on mid-training has focused on math, science reasoning, and software-engineering agents, leaving general agentic tool use comparatively understudied. MidTool generates synthetic training data that bridges the gap between pretraining corpora and the structured tool-calling patterns models need for agentic tasks. The study positions mid-training as a distinct and important phase for instilling specific capabilities before instruction fine-tuning begins.

stories.title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
stories.paragraph: This paper addresses how symbolic, auditable task models can be derived from passively recorded computer-use traces — sequences of screenshots paired with mouse and keyboard actions. As computer-use agents are deployed in real workplaces, organizations need interpretable representations of how tasks are actually performed so they can audit agent behavior and reuse learned procedures. The authors develop methods to induce such models from naturalistic traces without requiring manual annotation. The emphasis on auditability distinguishes this approach from end-to-end neural agents that embed task knowledge implicitly.

theme: Efficiency and Routing in AI Systems

stories.title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
stories.paragraph: This paper formalizes query routing across heterogeneous AI systems — multiple models, architectures, or inference-time settings — as an optimization problem where value estimation itself carries a cost. Cheap estimators such as embedding-based predictors are fast but noisy, while expensive evaluators are accurate but slow, creating a trade-off the authors model using a Pandora's box framework from economics. The work derives policies that decide when to pay for better estimates before committing a query to a specialist, balancing quality and efficiency. The approach is relevant to production systems where running every model on every query is cost-prohibitive.

stories.title: Information on trajectories: martingales and random times
stories.paragraph: This theoretical paper develops exact variational identities for nonnegative martingales by accounting for information flow along the path space, including at arbitrary random stopping times. The framework recovers classical concentration inequalities — ranging from Ville's inequality to PAC-Bayes bounds — as special cases and quantifies what each one discards relative to the exact identity. A key insight is that the tail controlled by any such bound is itself a relative entropy, which the authors decompose via the chain rule into per-step contributions. The work provides a unified information-theoretic lens for understanding a family of bounds widely used in machine learning theory.

stories.title: Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries
stories.paragraph: This paper addresses a calibration problem in sparse signal recovery: when a learned dictionary is highly coherent, the atom support selected by sparse pursuit may not have a unique physical interpretation, because alternative calibration-compatible dictionaries can assign different physical meanings to the same mathematical support. The authors develop resolution-aware physical-support inference that jointly accounts for dictionary uncertainty and measurement noise. The method produces confidence sets over physically meaningful supports rather than point estimates, providing uncertainty quantification aligned with the actual ambiguity in the calibration data. This is particularly relevant for applications such as sensor array processing where physical interpretability matters.

stories.title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
stories.paragraph: Researchers introduced G-CARL, a framework for generating patient-oriented interpretations of medical reports that balances clinical factuality with accessible communication. The system uses grounded, checklist-aligned reward learning to guide a medical vision-language model, ensuring generated text adheres to evidence in the report while adapting tone and complexity for a non-specialist audience. The authors also introduce a new benchmark task, Patient-oriented Medical Report Interpretation, to fill a gap they identify in existing medical vision-language evaluations. The dual requirement of factual grounding and patient-appropriate communication sets this task apart from standard medical report summarization.

stories.title: Explainable Transformer Models for Clinical Prediction Tasks on Structured Electronic Health Records
stories.paragraph: The paper presents BERT-LER, a BERT-style transformer pretrained and fine-tuned on a de-identified EHR dataset drawn from 75 million patients for clinical prediction tasks over structured health records. Unlike prior models, BERT-LER explicitly encodes quantitative laboratory values alongside coded medical events, addressing a common omission in EHR language models. The model is designed with interpretability in mind, producing attention-based explanations tied to specific input medical events. The scale of the pretraining corpus — 75 million patients — is one of the larger reported for a structured EHR model in the academic literature.

theme: Applied Machine Learning: Sensing and Prediction

stories.title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection
stories.paragraph: This study provides a controlled head-to-head comparison of three contact-free radio frequency technologies — FMCW radar, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi sensing — for monitoring human activity and detecting sleep interruptions in a bedroom setting. Prior work on RF-based healthcare monitoring rarely evaluates different radio technologies under identical hardware and deployment conditions, making cross-technology comparisons unreliable. All three sensors were ceiling-mounted in the same environment, enabling direct performance comparison on the same dataset. The results offer practitioners concrete guidance on technology selection for sleep and activity monitoring applications.

stories.title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
stories.paragraph: This paper proposes a three-agent pipeline that integrates conversational survey data collection, structured data processing, and behavioral demand prediction for transportation research. A chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey collected mode choice data from study participants, with subsequent agents handling preprocessing and model training. The system incorporates weather sensitivity into demand prediction, an often-overlooked factor in travel behavior modeling. By coupling data collection and modeling in a single agentic workflow, the approach reduces the fragmentation typical of transportation studies that develop each stage independently.

stories.title: $TCP_α$: Margin-Controlled Confidence estimation for reliable Music Information Retrieval
stories.paragraph: Researchers propose TCP-alpha, a post-hoc confidence estimation method that trains a lightweight auxiliary head over a frozen classifier to produce more reliable confidence scores for music information retrieval tasks. The method addresses the overconfidence problem common in deep neural networks, where high confidence scores are assigned even to incorrect predictions. Existing post-hoc targets suffer from label ambiguity that causes overlapping confidence assignments; TCP-alpha introduces margin control to sharpen the separation between confident correct and uncertain or incorrect predictions. The approach is evaluated in the specific domain of music information retrieval, where label ambiguity is particularly prevalent due to subjective genre and mood categories.

stories.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
stories.paragraph: Researchers have published a study questioning how language model self-improvement is measured, arguing that tracking which individual problems a model gains or loses between evaluations introduces vulnerability to measurement artifacts. The core issue is that differencing two noisy estimates of per-problem accuracy can produce spurious signals of improvement. To test this, the authors ran three rounds of rank-32 LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B and compared results against a frozen control model pushed through the identical pipeline, providing a concrete null baseline against which claimed gains can be audited. The work raises methodological concerns relevant to any research that judges self-training progress by problem-level transitions rather than aggregate accuracy.
